## The problem

Our team of twelve is spending more time managing merges than shipping value. Feature branches routinely live for two to three weeks, drifting far enough from main that integration becomes a dreaded event rather than a routine one. Code review happens too late to be useful — reviewers face 800-line diffs instead of digestible changes — and by the time a branch merges, the assumptions it was built on have often shifted underneath it. We've had three release-blocking merge conflicts in the last quarter alone, each costing a full day of two engineers' time to untangle.

## The proposal

I'm proposing we adopt trunk-based development: everyone commits directly to main at least once a day, behind feature flags where work isn't ready for users. Concretely, this means:

- Branches live no more than 1-2 days before merging back to main
- Incomplete features ship dark behind flags rather than sitting unintegrated
- CI must stay green on main at all times, enforced by pre-merge checks
- Code review shifts to small, incremental diffs reviewed within hours, not days
- We invest two weeks upfront in flag infrastructure and a faster CI pipeline before flipping the switch

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: trunk-based development demands discipline and tooling we don't fully have yet. If CI is flaky or slow, forcing frequent merges to a shaky main will multiply pain rather than reduce it, and a team without a mature feature-flag system risks shipping half-finished logic to production by accident. This isn't a hypothetical — teams that adopt trunk-based development without first hardening their pipeline often see a spike in production incidents in month one. I take this seriously, which is why the proposal includes a two-week investment in CI reliability and flagging before we cut over, not as an afterthought.

There's also a cultural risk: engineers accustomed to isolated branches may feel exposed committing unfinished work daily, and we'll need to normalize that discomfort explicitly as a team, not assume it resolves itself.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
